new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record (no catalog record and no stress statement held by the project for suii1243). Statement is tied to Central Sui (Sandong, Shuigen village) for the sketch; the sesquisyllabic examples come from eight data points (SD, DJ, PD, AT, TN, SY, JR, TZ) across Sui dialects. Consistent with the earlier independent reader's note in the mirror same passages, same reading).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Sui is a tone language (6 tones on unchecked syllables, 2 on checked) and largely monosyllabic; the only word-stress statement concerns sesquisyllabic words (reducing compounds / nominal prefixes such as kə0 ʔdjup7 'spirit', qa0- + noun): the minor (reduced) first syllable with schwa is always unstressed and carries a toneless 'neutral tone' (tone 0), the following major syllable is stressed and tone-bearing, i.e. an iambic (final-prominence) pattern within such words. No statement of stress placement for ordinary compounds or polysyllables beyond this.
new_statements.exceptions: Minor syllables 'almost always' precede the major syllable; schwa 'usually occurs without a coda only in a minor syllable and is therefore always short and unstressed' (p.19 / PDF 31); every minor syllable is identifiable with a full major syllable so an underlying tone 'can almost always be ascertained' (p.21 / PDF 33). Appendix G per-data-point phonology sketches (pp.227-254 / PDF 239-266) give initials, finals and tone values only, no stress statement; whole-book a full-text search for stress/accent|unstressed|iambic|accent|prominen|prosod finds linguistic stress statements only on pp.30-37 (other hits are 'accent' = regional accent, 'stress-free' test subjects, 'We stress that').
new_statements.identity_note: Sui [swi], Kam-Sui branch of Tai-Kadai, Sandu county, Guizhou; the phonology sketch is based on Central Sui as spoken in Shuigen village, Sandong township (data point SD, the traditional 'Sandong dialect' standard); the sesquisyllable examples are drawn from eight of the book's sixteen data points across Central, Western, Southern and other Sui dialect areas.

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A., John H. Esling, Jimmy G. Harris & James Wei. 2004. A phonetic study of Sui consonants and vowels [Glottolog title: '..consonants and tones']. Mon-Khmer Studies 34: 47-66.
sources.note: Instrumental study (tone plots, airflow, laryngoscopy) of Sandong Sui; §2 reviews Li 1948 / SDB 1956 / Zhang 1980 phonology (initials, 6 vowels, tones 1-8). The only 'stress' mentions (p.52) say the degree of stress and aspiration widens the glottal opening and lengthens VOT; nothing on where word stress falls.
